summary: I stopped at the tool check without reviewing s2e02. This session only has Read, Grep, Glob and StructuredOutput: there is no Bash to run the mechanical checks by script and no Write to save content/series2/episodes/s2e02/script.hi.json's review-notes.json, so the pass=false and score=0 here are placeholders, not a verdict on the script, and nothing should go back to S2.

medium: CLARITY (medium): l26 '[calm] Police में क्यों नहीं गए?' comes straight after l25, Nirala's 'दो साल से इंतज़ार है कि कोई असली अफ़सर इन्हें माँगे।'. It is easily heard as 'why didn't you take them to the police?'. 'नौ बार' then sounds like nine visits to the police, and only 'सीना एक centimetre कम' turns it into recruitment. This is the episode's key character reveal (bible b10: he failed the police entrance nine times), and the Hindi now differs from en l26 ('Why didn't you join the police?'). FIX, the same length (26 code points against 25), target unchanged at 2.6 s: l26 → '[calm] Police join क्यों नहीं की?' (Latin: 'Police join kyon nahin ki?'). Longer alternative, 3.2 s: '[calm] ख़ुद police में भर्ती क्यों नहीं हुए?' (Latin: 'Khud police mein bharti kyon nahin hue?'). The English needs no change.

CLARITY (medium): l14 '[quietly] दस minute।' Said by an SI to a suspect, a bare 'ten minutes' usually means an order ('you have ten minutes'). The fact the bible wants (b4: she has been timing him) is that he settled a theft in ten minutes, which her own thana never does. The clock insert does not settle which reading is meant. If it is heard as an ultimatum, the reveal is lost, and l29 then sounds as if she is backing off a ten-minute deadline. FIX: l14 → '[quietly] दस minute में।' (Latin: 'Das minute mein.'), 14 code points, target 1.6 s (+0.1 s, which makes target_total_seconds 133.9). It also gives this flagged short turn a carrier word (D-006 change 22). S5 mirror: en l14 → '[quietly] Ten minutes flat.' Not a protected line; the fact is still spoken.

CONTINUITY / STILLS-ONLY STAGING (medium): b8 shot 5 (l24) says 'her right index finger has gone down the column of entries'. The episode STATE and b8 shot 1 put the cuffs in her right hand from l03 to l28, with the helmet under her left arm. As written, the insert has no free hand to draw. FIX, action text only, no line change: 'Shot 5, l24: insert: the malkhana ledger open on the desk with the new entry written; her right index finger, the open cuffs hanging from the same hand across the page, has gone down the column of entries and stops on the last one.' This keeps the STATE and makes the cuffs over the ledger the image. S5 copies the action into script.en.json.

LENGTH (minor): the b12 silence (silent_seconds 1.8, before) has to carry the receiver lift, the dialling, one ring-back and the pick-up click (sfx_notes b12). One ring-back cadence is about a second of tone and two of gap, so the edit will likely need 3 s or more (estimate). Trim step (1) in writer_notes would cut this hold to 1.0 s, where that sound cannot fit. FIX, either option: (a) the sfx becomes 'receiver lifted, the last two digits, one short ring-back burst, the click' and the 1.8 s stays; or (b) set b12 silent_seconds to 3.0, which makes target_total_seconds 135.0 in hi and 125.6 in en. In both cases trim step (1) applies to the b11 hold only.

METADATA (minor): the writer_notes 'Open point for S3' about the neighbour's voice is out of date. D-019 settled it: l10 stays with neighbour_voice, as a call from the bench, voiced by an existing minor voice (door3_man by default). FIX: the note cites D-019 and drops the Pushpa fallback. I did not reopen the ruling. Separate, and S1's job rather than this script's: the bible errata D-019 ordered has not landed. bible.json voices_only (lines 184 to 189) has no neighbour_voice, and the s2e02 entry in the silent list (line 192) still says the neighbours do not speak.

PERFORMABILITY (minor): l15 '[nervous] भैयाजी। Madam... lockup में। मतलब... छुपिए।' puts [nervous] and two ellipses on a voice whose note says 'Frightened is a thin, steady voice, not a stammer'. My guess, not measured on this cast, is that v4 will add a stammer or breaths. No script change: if the take stammers, S10 swaps the tag to [quietly] and keeps the text, as the writer notes already allow.

CONTINUITY (optional): in s2e03, Pushpa says she heard 'talkies' and then 'फिर दरवाज़ा बंद।'. In s2e02 b11 she leaves slowly, and nothing in b12 shows a door that is still open. Optional, action only: b12 shot 1 adds 'the door behind him left a hand's width open'. Pushpa is not shown.
critic_rerun.summary:
s2e02 passes at 8.0 with nothing fatal and no must-fix items, so under D-019 it goes to storyboard and voice. Six of the eight checks were not run as the skill asks, by script: I had no shell. They were done by hand and Grep, the JSON was not parsed, and no character count was made by a tool.

Files read: <repo>/content/series2/episodes/s2e02/script.hi.json in full, and script.en.json for ids, speakers, tags, targets, on_screen and silences. Against them: bible.json (the s2e02 beats b1 to b12, the key lines, cliffhanger ladder, props and locations, the voices_only and silent lists, the names rule and the no-narrator set-up), D-004, D-006, D-016 and D-019, the s2e01 and s2e03 seams, and the s2e02 entries in continuity.json. I did not read branch-map.md. Its content is regenerated from the bible, which I read directly.

critic round 1. Text for S2 to save word for word into the critic section of <repo>/content/series2/episodes/s2e02/review-notes.json. Merge it in and keep the existing continuity section.

VERDICT: pass, no fatal problem, 8.0. Sub-scores: hook 8, stakes 7, choice null, branch_distinct 8, cliffhanger 8.5, hinglish 8.5, performability 8, length 7.5, continuity 8.5. File: content/series2/episodes/s2e02/script.hi.json, with script.en.json.

CHECKS RUN (by hand and Grep; no tool parse or count):
- JSON: not parsed. Pattern searches on both files found no comma before a closing bracket, no missing comma at a line break, no two objects side by side without a comma, no tab or backslash, and no stray double quote inside a string. Searches are not a parse.
- Ids: every speaker is in the bible's characters (nandini, nirala, pushpa, bhaiyaji, tripathi), except neighbour_voice, which stands by D-019's ruling (the bible errata is still pending). Every location is in the bible (projection_room, talkies_lobby, real_thana).
- Tags: emotion_tags match the inline tags on all 34 lines in hi and all 34 in en, checked one by one. l10 is untagged, and so is its list.
- Durations, hi: 120.4 s spoken, plus 22 speaker changes at 0.3 s (6.6 s), plus 6.8 s of silence, is 133.8 s, equal to target_total_seconds. en: 111.0 + 6.6 + 6.8 = 124.4, equal to its target.
- Line count: 34.
- Characters: my hand count is 1,040 if each nukta letter counts as one. The file stores nuktas decomposed: U+093C appears 10 times in 8 dialogue lines, and there is no precomposed U+0958 to U+095F. That makes about 1,050 code points (the writer has 1,039 and about 1,050). This is at D-016's measure and under D-019's 1,100 trigger.
- Density: 8.6 characters a second overall. The densest line is l32 at 9.75, none is over 12, and the sparsest is l24 at 4.3 (one word).
- Parity: hi and en have the same 11 beat ids (b1 to b8 and b10 to b12; there is no b9, as the bible says), the same 34 line ids, the same speakers in the same order, and the same on_screen and silence values.
- Lead: on screen in 8 of 11 beats (not b7, b11 or b12); she speaks 9 of the 34 lines.
- Bookish forms: no यह or वह, and none of किन्तु, परन्तु, कृपया, तथा or एवं. No bare 'साहब'. 'Inspector साहब' comes only from Bhaiyaji (l16, l17), and the town's 'निराला जी' is heard first (l10).
- Tag placement: no ellipsis straight after a tag, no dash cut-offs, no whispers. The cliffhanger is fully voiced, with no phone filter, and the bed ducks under it.
- Key lines: every bible key line for s2e02 is spoken, in the bible's wording or in the trims listed in writer_notes. Protected lines are word for word: l05 to l09, l13, l17, l33 and l34.
- Seams: s2e01 ends on 'तो कल दस बजे से पहले... arrest किसे करूँ?', with her hand on the pouch and token seven on her right wrist. s2e02 b1 opens on exactly that, and the S4 token fix is in place (pocketed on l03). s2e03 opens at 10:30 p.m. on Bhaiyaji's call. l17 keeps 'त्रिपाठी जी से सस्ते भी, मीठे भी।', which s2e03 now depends on (D-016 direction 9).
- Shots: every beat with more than one shot maps its lines to shots. The longest single-shot line is l06 at 6.8 s, and l17 (7.2 s) is split across two shots. No frame has more than two sheet faces. Motion is written as sound: the stamp, the car door, the keys leaving, the dialling.

WHY THE SCORES:
- Hook 8: there is no recap. Nirala's 'Arrest आपका हक़ है, madam।' answers the line s2e01 ended on, and 'charge handover' lands by about 5 to 8 s on the targets. It lands nearer 4 s in the casting take, which ran l01 and l02 in 4.88 s (D-019).
- Stakes 7: the threat to Nirala (l15) and the case (l33 and l34) is clear, but her own deadline comes back only at l29, about 100 s in. That is acceptable for a shared middle episode, so no fix is asked.
- Branch distinct 8: the episode loads both sides of the s2e03 vote. Nirala's sincerity and his 'नौ बार' make arresting him costly. Bhaiyaji's trust in his 'Inspector साहब' makes the sting possible, and his menace makes it dangerous. The say-it-aloud plant (l13) pays off in both branches.
- Cliffhanger 8.5: it is spoken in the room, cut before any answer, and set up by Pushpa's l09 ('ना भैयाजी को'). The ending_question is not answered on screen.
- Hinglish 8.5: lines are short, each voice keeps its own register, and English nouns sit in Hindi grammar. Two clarity points, l26 and l14, are in the medium list.
- Performability 8: Nirala carries 14 of the [calm] tags, which suits him. Every tag from the verify group has a fallback.
- Length 7.5: the targets are honest, and if anything slow. The total sits 14 s over the 120 s aim but inside D-019's 150 s ceiling. The writer_notes trim order exists and spares the protected lines.
- Continuity 8.5: knowledge, props, wardrobe, time of day and places all hold, with one hand-staging slip in b8 shot 5.

PROBLEMS AND FIXES: see the medium list. That is 3 medium items, 3 minor and 1 optional. None touches another episode, the s2e03 seam, a glimpse, a lock or a balance line. If S2 applies the l14 or b8 fixes, S5 mirrors them in script.en.json. The l26 fix is Hindi only.

ESTIMATES (labelled as such): the real finished cut is about 125 to 145 s. At the proof's measured 8.4 characters a second it comes to about 137 s, and this cast's casting takes ran shorter. Hook timing is an estimate. The b12 sound needs about 3 s, also an estimate.

NOT VERIFIED: no JSON parse; no count by a tool (mine is by hand, with perhaps 1 per cent error); no take heard; no frame seen. The English was checked for structure, tags, targets and the meaning of l14 and l26, not for idiom line by line, which rests on S5. The neighbour-voice ruling (D-019) was applied, not reopened. The bible's voices_only list and its s2e02 silent note are still uncorrected; that is S1's errata.
